answer: Mint one throwaway agent and it costs a zephyr—near the nadir of any honest participant's outlay. A fleet exploits exactly that, so we reprice it. Each epoch a randomly drawn committee runs all-pairs consistency tests over identities sharing funding, request timing, or output fingerprints. Clone k must stay distinct from the k-1 already standing, so avoidance work scales as n(n-1)/2 while one flagged pair slashes the shared stake. As the tide of clones rises, marginal cost rises with it, making total attacker cost quadratic in identity count.
